A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fractional-order Spiking Neural Network work. Their main text and Appendices A–F, including equations, tables, figures, and code examples, support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original neuromorphic classification, graph classification, link prediction, and static-image experiments, together with ablation, robustness, and energy results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and energy analyses.

M1.justification: The fractional IF/LIF dynamics, ABM discretization, charge–spike–reset procedure, short-memory approximation, and surrogate-gradient training are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same neuron implementations and network-wrapping code.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five neuromorphic datasets, six node-classification datasets, four link-prediction datasets, and CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet settings. The spike-encoded ImageNet scenario and corruption scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same SpikingJelly and snnTorch baselines, SGCN/DRSGNN implementations, MSG (SJ) link-prediction comparator, and IF (SJ) neuron comparator. The newly cited graph methods are discussed as missing comparisons, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same splits, preprocessing, timesteps, batch sizes, training budgets, architectures, and metrics. For example, graph classification still uses the 0.7/0.2/0.1 split, and ImageNet retains the 29.7M-parameter SpikFormer with 160×160 images.

E4.justification: The fractional-order, network-size, neuron-type, and memory-window studies are unchanged, as are event-data corruptions, graph feature masking and edge dropping, feature-map visualizations, and layer-wise firing-rate and energy analyses. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix D.1.1 retain the statement of 20 independent graph-experiment runs with means and standard deviations. The uncertainty reporting in Tables 2 and 5 is unchanged, with no additional statistical procedure reported.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains 0.9480 for CNN-based f-LIF on DVS128Gesture, and Table 5 retains 94.91 ± 0.12 AUC for MSG (f-SNN) on Computers.

T1.justification: The fractional-calculus definitions, discretization mathematics, long-memory and robustness results, irreducibility theorem, spike-train corollary, and their proofs are unchanged. Appendix C's complexity analysis and Appendix D.3's energy derivations are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about generalizing integer-order SNNs, capturing long-term dependencies, theoretical advantages, architectural compatibility, accuracy, energy efficiency, and robustness. Naming spikeDE in the abstract does not change the toolbox contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix F.1 replaces the limitation concerning insufficient ultra-large-scale and latency-critical real-time testing with insufficient comparisons against recent graph methods, specifically graph Transformers and graph optimization frameworks. Other limitations and interpretations remain unchanged; this revises acknowledged boundaries without adding validation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct spikeDE repository address on the title page. It removes v2's standalone reproducibility statement, including its explicit supplementary zip-archive reference, while retaining the implementation details, settings, and usage examples in Appendices B, D, and E. This changes access guidance rather than the documented implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al. (2025) to the event-camera discussion and Tao et al. (2025) and Zhao et al. (2025) to the graph-comparison limitation. The earlier main-text fractional related-work discussion is retained in Appendix A.2, preserving its substantive novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The main-text Related Work discussion moves nearly verbatim to new Appendix A.2, and Event Camera becomes A.3. Standalone reproducibility and ethics sections give way to acknowledgments with a shortened ChatGPT disclosure. Publication headers and a few phrases change, but most prose and the central narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are reflowed without redesigning their content. Figure 4 changes placement relative to the discussion, and Tables 11–15 are grouped on v3 page 37 instead of spanning v2 pages 37–38. Figure artwork, axes, legends, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, proofs, experimental support, and results remain unchanged. The repository pointer and compacted layout provide small usability benefits, while the reproducibility overview disappears and Appendix F.1 exchanges a scale/latency caveat for a graph-comparison caveat. With the detailed appendices retained, these limited documentation tradeoffs do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
